what: The 101 Squadron IAF Supermarine Spitfire LF Mk IXe as flown from October 1948, built from primitives (lofted sections, a NACA 22xx wing on an elliptical clipped planform) by tools/spitfire_101_model.py in Blender 5.2.2 LTS (pip bpy); markings painted into the colour map by a colour function of each texel's 3D point. No third-party model, image or scan; no AI.

sources.length_9.47_m: en.wikipedia 'Supermarine Spitfire variants: specifications, performance and armament', LF Mk IXe, read 2026-11-05
sources.planform_11.23_m_ellipse: en.wikipedia 'Supermarine Spitfire', read 2026-11-05 (the full wing's span, the ellipse clipped at 9.9 m; dihedral 6 deg, NACA 2213/2209.4, incidence +2/-0.5 deg)
sources.markings: Yoav Efrati, Colors & Markings of the Israeli Air Force (IAF, 2005) pp. 6, 12, 14, as cited in UnitModels.Spitfire and docs/units.md
sources.band_white_blue_white_ahead_of_fin: Efrati p. 4 (the IAF command's order of 31 May 1948), read 2026-11-08 at http://files.iaflibrary.org.il/DigitalLibrary/English/ColorsMarkings.pdf (PDF page 5)
sources.insignia_101_sqn: Efrati p. 11 (PDF page 12): Stan Andrews' winged skull wearing a flying cap, red, white and black, on the S-199's left nose section (caption and two photographs); p. 12 (PDF page 13): on the Spitfires 'to the left side of their airplanes'. Drawn from primitives, not traced
sources.span_9.9_m: en.wikipedia 'Supermarine Spitfire variants: specifications, performance and armament', clipped LF Mk IXe 32 ft 6 in (9.9 m), read 2026-11-05
sources.four_blades: docs/units.md (IAF Museum Mk IX, Hatzerim, Commons CC BY 2.5)

design_values: fuselage sections, canopy, radiators, intake, exhausts, tailplane and fin sizes, hub position, propeller diameter and blade shape, roundel sizes and places, wing-roundel star orientation, rudder stripe angle and width, the rear-fuselage band's place and stripe width, the insignia's size, place and shape proportions, camouflage pattern, demarcation line, panel lines
